body.p: The Examiner has rejected claims 1-3, 6-8, 17-19, 22-24, 31 and 45 under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(2) as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent Publication No. 2020/0110194 to Young et al. ("Young") in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2005/0124864 to Mack et al. ("Mack"); rejected claims 9 and 25 under 35 U.S.C. §103 as allegedly being unpatentably obvious over Young in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2020/0146910 to Demirli et al. ("Demirli"); rejected claims 10 and 26 under 35 U.S.C. §103 as allegedly being unpatentably obvious over Young in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2014/037163 5 to Shinar et al. ("Shinar").

Summary of Amendments. With this amendment, claims 1, 3, 9, 10, 17, 19, 25, 26, 31, and 45 have been amended. Claim 2 is canceled, without prejudice or disclaimer. The amendments to the claims are fully supported by the application as filed, and no new matter has been added.

Claims 1-3, 6-8, 17-19, 22-24, 31, and 45 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being allegedly unpatentable over Young in view of Mack. The remaining claims stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being allegedly unpatentable over Young in view of Mack and additional references. Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.
Claim 1 has recites a system comprising, inter alia, an apparatus configured to separate into components each of a plurality of physiological signals received from a plurality of sensors, wherein
the separating comprises:
pre-processing each of the plurality of physiological signals to generate, for
each of the plurality of physiological signals,
specifying a state space of model parameters, each of the model parameters
of the state space describing an aspect of the plurality physiological signals,
determining a posterior distribution of the physiological signals given the
respective vectors and the state space of model parameters,
determining a change in at least a first parameter of the model parameters of
the state space,
determining if the change in at least the first parameter of the model
parameters of the state space is below a predefined threshold, and in response to the change in the at least the first model parameter being less than the predefined
threshold, and
using the posterior distribution to estimate, for each of the plurality of
physiological signals, waveforms of the separated components ...
Young, taken alone or in combination with Mack, fails to teach or suggest at least the above noted features of claim 1.

The Examiner relies on Young at paragraph [0047] as allegedly teaching "separating into components each of the plurality of physiological signals..." Applicant disagrees. Young at para. [0047] and elsewhere is silent with respect to the features of claim 1 described above. Mack is similarly silent with respect to these features of claim 1. As such, Young fails to disclose or suggest any separating into components each of a plurality of physiological signals received from a plurality of sensors, "wherein the separating comprises pre-processing each of the plurality of physiological signals to generate, for each of the plurality of physiological signals, specifying a state space of model parameters, each of the model parameters of the state space describing an aspect of the plurality physiological signals, determining a posterior distribution of the physiological signals, determining a change in at least a first parameter of the model parameters of the state space, determining if the change in at least the first parameter of the model parameters of the state space is below a predefined threshold, and in response to the change in the at least the first model parameter being below the predefined threshold, using the posterior distribution to estimate, for each of the plurality of physiological signals, waveforms of the separated components ..." as amended claim 1 recites. And Mack fails to cure this deficiency.

In view of the foregoing, claim 1 is thus patentable over Young, taken alone or in combination with Mack. Claims 17, 31, and 45 recite subject matter substantially similar to that of claim 1. At least for the reasons discussed with respect to claim 1, claims 17, 31, and 45 are patentable over Young, taken alone or in combination with Mack.

Claim 2 has been cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer, thus rendering moot its rejection. The remaining claims depend, either directly or indirectly, from one of claims 1, 17, 31, and 45, and are thus patentable over Young, taken alone or in combination with Mack or any of the other cited references, by virtue of their dependencies at least.
In view of the foregoing, the rejections 35 U.S.C. § 103 should be withdrawn.

On the basis of the foregoing amendments, the pending claims are in condition for allowance. It is believed that all of the pending claims have been addressed in this paper. However, failure to address a specific rejection, issue or comment, does not signify agreement with or concession of that rejection, issue or comment. In addition, because the arguments made above are not intended to be exhaustive, there may be reasons for patentability of any or all pending claims (or other claims) that have not been expressed. Finally, nothing in this paper should be construed as an intent to concede any issue with regard to any claim, except as specifically stated in this paper.

No fees are believed to be due with this response other than those indicated on the fee transmittal. However, the Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees that may be due, or credit any overpayment of same, to Deposit Account 50-0311, Reference No. 37866- 639N01US/2018-330-2.
